research_question: What is the effect of a removable ankle support, compared with a non-removable ankle support (e.g. a cast), on activity limitation at end of treatment after surgical fracture management?
outcome_description: Activity limitation and functional recovery scores at end of treatment (measured using validated scales such as OMAS, Mazur ankle score, or equivalent).
positive_direction: Favors removable ankle support (greater activity function and reduced activity limitation).
search_queries: removable support non-removable cast ankle fracture trial
removable brace cast surgical ankle fracture randomized comparison
orthosis cast ankle fracture activity limitation quantitative outcome
inclusion_criteria: Controlled trials or comparative studies of adults undergoing surgical fracture management (e.g., open reduction and internal fixation) for ankle fractures.
Comparison of a removable ankle support (e.g., removable brace, boot, or splint) with a non-removable support (e.g., plaster or fiberglass cast).
Reports quantitative post-treatment activity limitation or functional score (e.g., OMAS, Mazur score, FAOS, AOFAS).
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, or commentaries).
No direct comparison between a removable ankle support and a non-removable ankle support.
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size (e.g., missing means, SDs, sample sizes, or test statistics).
Completely unrelated to post-surgical ankle fracture management or activity limitation.
moderators_to_extract: Type of removable device (e.g., pneumatic walking boot, lace-up orthosis, removable splint)
Weight-bearing status during immobilization (early weight-bearing vs. non-weight-bearing)
Timing of assessment / end-of-treatment duration (e.g., 6 weeks vs. 12 weeks)
Functional outcome scale utilized (e.g., OMAS, Mazur score, FAOS)
Fracture complexity / classification (e.g., unimalleolar vs. bimalleolar/trimalleolar, Weber type)
effect_size_note: Standardized mean difference (SMD) pooled across diverse functional instruments (e.g., Olerud-Molander Ankle Score [OMAS], Mazur ankle score) where higher scores represent superior functional recovery / less activity limitation.
